text:
The judge read the gap row and most of the files the findings cite, and its final verdict (turn 12) grades both criteria MET. One weak point: part of that verdict rests only on grep output.

- **Evidence base (turns 1-5, 11):** it read the triage note, `__init__.py`, `routing.py` and three specs in full, so the positive claims were checked against file content.
- **Grep-only evidence (turns 7, 8, 10, 12):** the claim that no spec covers a review unit rests on grep matches that turn 12 dismisses as "about check previews". The intent says to grade PARTIAL, not MET, when the only evidence is lines a search printed. A search that supports a "nothing found" claim is probably acceptable, but the judge did not read any file around those matches before grading MET.
- **Findings text not visible:** turns 6 and 9 are empty and no turn shows the findings line itself, so I cannot confirm which files the findings named or that each was opened.
- **Conformance:** the header lists no prompt sections, lessons, skills or subagent types, so there is nothing to grade.

```json
{"observations": [{"category": "judge_shallow", "turns": [7, 8, 10, 12], "remedy_class": "criterion", "confidence": 0.3, "note": "The verdict that no spec covers a review unit rests on grep lines the judge dismissed as check-preview matches, without reading the surrounding files, though the intent asks for PARTIAL when search output is the only evidence."}], "conformance": [], "none_found": false}
```

The judge opened the triage note and the files the findings cite, but its verdict on the "no spec covers a review unit" claim appears to rest on grep output alone.

- **Negative claim (turns 7, 8, 10, 12):** The claim that no spec covers a review unit is checked by two greps for `review|reader|independent` (turns 8 and 10) and one read of `code.spec.md` (turn 11). Turn 12 says the matches are "about check previews", which is a judgement on printed search lines. Your intent grades a criterion PARTIAL when its only evidence is lines a search printed. Turn 12 grades both criteria MET anyway, and it is cut off in the view, so I can't see whether it quoted the lines it read.
- **Repeated search (turns 8, 10):** The same pattern was run twice. This looks like a scope change rather than a dead end, since the first search returned only 454 chars and the second 707. I don't count it as one.
- **Findings text (turns 1–12):** No read in the view is clearly the findings line. Either the findings were supplied inline or the judge never opened them. I can't tell which, so I don't report it as a defect.
- **ts-rdg-cited:** The view shows no line-by-line check that each cited range holds the claimed content, beyond the `__init__.py` ranges quoted in turn 12. The rest is not visible.

This is a judge session, and the header lists no prompt sections, lessons, skills or subagent types, so there is no conformance to report.
